record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Ordered and Orderable Groups
record.original_question: If every ℓ-subgroup of an ℓ-group G is closed, then is G discrete?

evidence.quote: 1.40∗ . If every ℓ-subgroup of an ℓ-group G is closed, then is G discrete?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a lattice-ordered group (an $\ell$-group): a group equipped with a lattice order $\le$ such that the group operation is order-preserving in both arguments (equivalently, $a(b\vee c)d = abd \vee acd$ and $a(b\wedge c)d = abd\wedge acd$ for all $a,b,c,d\in G$). An $\ell$-subgroup of $G$ is a subgroup that is also a sublattice with respect to $\vee$ and $\wedge$. An $\ell$-subgroup $H\le G$ is called closed if, for every subset $S\subseteq H$ that has a supremum (respectively infimum) in $G$, that supremum (respectively infimum) lies in $H$. The $\ell$-group $G$ is called discrete if for every $g\in G$ with $g>e$ there exists an element $h\in G$ such that $e<h\le g$ and there is no $x\in G$ with $e<x<h$ (i.e., $G$ has atoms above the identity covering every strictly positive element; equivalently, every strictly positive element dominates a cover of the identity).

Prove or disprove: if every $\ell$-subgroup of $G$ is closed in the above sense, then $G$ is discrete.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return any source establishing or refuting the implication that an $\ell$-group all of whose $\ell$-subgroups are closed must be discrete. No subsequent solution or counterexample was located in the available literature, so the current status appears unresolved.
